work_packages.title: Probabilistic multi-sensor diagnosis of the field state
work_packages.description: Build and calibrate the diagnostic branch: acquire and harmonise Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical (and optional PlanetScope) with soil-sensor, weather and field-observation data; implement Route A (direct one-step probabilistic fusion via a Bayesian hierarchical model / Gaussian process) and/or Route B (homogeneous-patch proxy) to estimate the latent field state (root-zone soil moisture, crop water stress, canopy) as a posterior with honest uncertainty. Route scope (RQ2) and target field state (RQ3) are open decisions.

work_packages.title: Uncertainty-aware decision engine and demonstrator integration
work_packages.description: Build the prognostic branch and decision engine: uncertainty-aware AquaCrop calibration retaining an honest parameter posterior; counterfactual irrigation simulation over weather ensembles; profit-based decision recommendation under uncertainty. Integrate diagnosis and decision into a standalone research demonstrator (web MVP). Decision objective (RQ6) and TRL target (RQ10) are open decisions.

work_packages.title: Field validation, ground truth and uncertainty calibration
work_packages.description: Design and run the validation protocol: collect ground truth (RQ4), assess uncertainty calibration - e.g. whether 90% prediction intervals contain the truth about 90% of the time (RQ5), define pilot-success criteria (RQ7), and test Route B's patch-covariation assumption, including the control-stand variant (RQ9). Validation sites, farms and data-provider arrangements are Unresolved (spine-dependent).
work_packages.note: Research content Confirmed; the specific validation sites and field partners are Unresolved (Unconfirmed Partner Placeholders METH-PART-006).

work_packages.title: Training, supervision and two-way transfer of knowledge
work_packages.description: MSCA-PF structural work package for the researcher's training (scientific, management, transferable skills), supervision, and two-way transfer of knowledge between researcher and host. Content: a Career Development Plan prepared jointly by supervisor and fellow and submitted as a project deliverable at the start of the action (by months 2-3), then reviewed and updated at M12/M24; >=120 hours of transferable-skills training covering the MSCA-PF mandatory dimensions - digital and AI skills (including responsible use of generative AI in environmental modelling and scientific coding), knowledge valorisation, innovation and entrepreneurship, research integrity, and open science / FAIR data stewardship; supervision through regular research reviews at the host's environmental-physics / geoinformatics group; two-way transfer of knowledge - the fellow contributes the uncertainty-aware calibration method and probabilistic-fusion expertise, and takes up the host's geoinformatics and field-validation competences, evidenced by >=2 methods seminars delivered at the host; co-supervision of >=1 MSc thesis.
